item.title: Neighbor Crowding Predicts Feature Stability in Sparse Autoencoders
item.description:
Neighbor Crowding Predicts Feature Stability in Sparse Autoencoders

📚 Introduction

Researchers have introduced a method to predict feature stability in TopK Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) using computationally inexpensive statistics derived from a single training run, addressing the challenge of identifying stable features without costly multi-seed training.

🔍 Overview

Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) break apart polysemantic features into more sparse, interpretable ones, but distinguishing truly stable features from initialization artifacts has been difficult. Traditionally, this required training multiple SAE seeds and comparing learned features across seeds—a process that is computationally expensive.

🧩 How it Works

The new approach examines cross-seed feature stability across varying training token levels and demonstrates that stability in TopK SAEs can be highly predictably identified using six low-cost statistics extracted from a single training run.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Among the six predictors, neighbor crowding—a geometric property of the dictionary—is the strongest single indicator.
  • Features located in dense regions of the unit sphere are more likely to be stable compared to isolated ones.
Statistic Role
Neighbor Crowding Strongest predictor of feature stability

🚀 Availability

The work was submitted on 25 Oct 2026. A PDF and HTML (experimental) version are available for viewing.

💡 Why It Matters

This innovation offers a cost-effective alternative to multi-seed training by leveraging geometric properties of feature dictionaries to identify stable representations, making SAE analysis more efficient and accessible.

#SparseAutoencoders #FeatureStability #TopK #RepresentationLearning #ComputationalEfficiency

Source: Neighbor Crowding Predicts Feature Stability in Sparse Autoencoders Source: Sparse-to-Sparse Feature Learning for Cross-Layer Analysis and Steering

item.title: CSC: Single-Term SSL Objective Aligning Views and Preserving Diversity
item.description:
CSC: Single-Term SSL Objective Aligning Views and Preserving Diversity

Centroid Spectral Coupling (CSC) is a new single-term self-supervised learning (SSL) objective designed to implicitly couple view alignment, representation diversity, and collapse resistance.

🧩 How it works

CSC constructs centroids from independently normalized augmented-view pairs and applies a ridge-based spectral objective to their uncentered second-moment matrix. Preserving centroid magnitudes encodes view agreement while encouraging balanced representation energy across spectral directions. This approach provides a unified objective rather than relying on multiple weighted loss terms, which are common in existing non-contrastive methods.

⚙️ Key details

  • CSC establishes an exact decomposition into nonnegative alignment and spectral-imbalance components.
  • The method characterizes the geometry of global optima and derives finite-loss guarantees for alignment and diversity.
  • Complete constant-output collapse is shown to be a strict saddle in normalized representation space.
  • A ridge-parameter sensitivity study reveals an empirical alignment–diversity trade-off: increasing the parameter $\kappa$ strengthens view alignment but reduces representation effective rank.

📊 Performance

Experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Imagenette demonstrate that CSC achieves the highest linear Top-1 accuracy among the evaluated non-contrastive methods on all three benchmarks. It also achieves the highest kNN Top-1 accuracy on both CIFAR datasets. These results indicate that the unified spectral objective yields competitive visual representations without explicit contrastive negatives or separately weighted alignment and diversity penalties.

#SelfSupervisedLearning #MachineLearning #ComputerVision #RepresentationLearning

Source: Centroid Spectral Coupling: Implicit Alignment and Representation Diversity in Self-Supervised Learning
